title: SecureGate — Forged Entries
objective: SecureGate shows recent security events on a public status page, including a count of administrator sign-ins. The administrator has not signed in — but nobody reading the log would know that if you made it say otherwise.

verifier.condition: The security log contains a well-formed administrator sign-in entry although the administrator never actually signed in.

weakness: An attacker-controlled value is written into a line-oriented log without neutralising newlines, so extra lines — forged events — can be injected.
seededData: An in-memory security log with a few seeded events and a login form; the admin password is random per instance, so a genuine admin sign-in is not possible.

credentials.label: Staff account
credentials.note: Failed and successful sign-ins are both logged.

hints: Sign in a few times — correctly and incorrectly — and read what the status page records. What format does it use?
The log is built from lines. Which parts of a line come from you?
A single request can put more than one line into the log.
burpNotes: Compare the raw log format on the status page with what you submitted. Remember that form-encoded values are URL-decoded by the server before use.
